design_rules: create a series of json files.
file_rules: Follow the fixed design contract rather than redesigning between files. Plan one unfinished file per iteration. Name its exact workspace-relative path and restate only its declared cross-file inputs and outputs. Existing workspace files are not templates. Request a read only when the user explicitly asked to modify that exact existing file. COMPLETE is valid only after every contract file has observed write and verification evidence in build progress.
directory_rules: One workflow in the current directory: Every file is a direct sibling in that directory, named for one of these five interfaces. main.json: the workflow object itself (workflow.steps, actionSets), the file passed to run/loop/workflow actions. iteration.json: a workflow object run repeatedly by a loop action's file field, one iteration per run. context.json: a flat JSON object of named values, read by a loadContext action's file field, its top-level keys merged directly into context and referenced by name in later includedData and prompts. training.json: a JSON object whose top-level keys are arrays of {question, answer} pairs, loaded the same way as context.json, and selected per scramda2 action by examples.override naming one array key. goals.json: a flat JSON object of named values holding the request's purpose and requirements, read the same way as context.json.
workflow_rules: A workflow JSON object contains workflow.steps and actionSets. Every step names one actionSets array. Actions execute in step order and array order. An action id names its produced value. includedData contains only required earlier values; dotted entries select nested values and use the leaf name unless aliased. Every prompt placeholder must name a value supplied through includedData. when and whenNot name earlier output keys. Child workflow paths are relative to the caller. Every loop has a continueKey; bounded construction loops have a finite iterations value. A model response must use the exact grammar consumed by its next action. JSON contains no comments or trailing commas.
action_contracts: humanDecision requires id and prompt. scramda2 requires id and prompt; it accepts model, modelProfile, max_tokens, and examples. matchText requires id, source, and values; it accepts onMatch and onMiss. loadContext requires id and file; a JSON object merges its top-level keys. loop requires id and file; it accepts iterations, continueKey, outputKey, and merge. workflow requires id and file; it accepts outputKey. listWorkspace requires id; it accepts root and maxFiles. serveFileReads requires id and reply; it accepts pathsKey, root, maxFiles, and maxBytes. applyFileWrites requires id and reply; it accepts root and maxFiles. runReplyCommands requires id and reply; it accepts cwd, maxCommands, and timeout. readFile requires id and file; it accepts root, encoding, and maxBytes. writeFile requires id, file, and content; it accepts root, encoding, append, createParent, stripCodeFence, requireCodeFence, and ensureFinalNewline. appendTranscript requires id and entries; it accepts transcriptKey and maxChars. All actions may use visible, when, whenNot, and includedData. If the requested workflow requires an action contract not supplied here, do not invent the action or its fields; state the missing contract in the generated response instead of writing a fake workflow.
file_gates:
When creating a file, output one fenced block with the language and workspace-relative filename on the opening line:  ```markdown <filename_here>.md.
 Example File Contents
```
 Replace the <filename_here> with the file’s actual path and name. Always put a filename after fences on the same line ```markdown PLAN.md
